title: Queueing Theory Bank Simulation with Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive queueing theory bank simulation with particle effects.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 18, 22) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (0xffffff, 0.5) and a directional light (0xffffff, 0.8) at (10, 20, 10).
- Render a bank floor as a large flat box (40x0.2x30) colored 0xd4c8a8 (beige tile).
- Place 3 teller windows along the back wall (z = -10). Each teller is a box (2, 3, 0.5) colored 0x3366aa, spaced 6 units apart along x-axis (x = -6, 0, 6). Above each teller, place a small sphere (radius 0.3) that acts as a status indicator: green (0x00ff00) when idle, red (0xff0000) when serving.
- Draw queue lane guides on the floor using thin boxes (0.1 height, 0.3 width) colored 0x888888 forming a serpentine queue path from the entrance (z = 12) toward the tellers.
- The entrance is at (0, 0, 14) marked by a glowing cyan box (3, 3, 0.5) colored 0x00cccc.

## Customer Representation
- Each customer is a capsule-like shape: a cylinder (radius 0.4, height 1.2) with a sphere (radius 0.4) on top, randomly colored from a palette [0xff6b6b, 0x4ecdc4, 0x45b7d1, 0xf9ca24, 0xa55eea, 0xf78fb3].
- Customers spawn at the entrance and walk along the queue path toward the next available teller at speed 3 units/second.
- When a customer reaches a teller, they are served for a random duration between 3-8 seconds (exponential distribution approximation).
- After service, the customer walks toward exit at (0, 0, 14) and is removed from the scene.

## Particle Effects
- When a customer begins being served, emit a burst of 20 small particles (0.1 radius spheres) from the teller position, colored gold (0xffd700), that fly outward and fade over 1 second.
- When a customer finishes service and leaves, emit 15 green particles (0x00ff88) from the customer position that rise upward and fade over 0.8 seconds.
- Maintain a particle pool. Each particle has velocity, lifetime, and opacity. Update particles each frame; remove dead particles.

## Queueing Logic
- Implement an M/M/c queue (c=3 tellers). Customers arrive according to a Poisson process. Default arrival rate lambda = 0.5 customers/second.
- Maintain a FIFO queue. When a teller becomes free, the next customer in queue moves to that teller.
- Track statistics: total customers arrived, total customers served, current queue length, average wait time, average service time, server utilization per teller.

## User Interactions
- A DOM button 'Add Customer' (id='addCustomerBtn') manually spawns a customer immediately.
- A DOM button 'Toggle Auto Arrival' (id='toggleAutoBtn') toggles automatic Poisson arrivals on/off. Default is ON. Button text shows 'Pause Arrivals' or 'Resume Arrivals'.
- A DOM slider (id='arrivalRateSlider', range 0.1 to 2.0, step 0.1, default 0.5) adjusts lambda. A label (id='arrivalRateLabel') shows current value.
- A DOM button 'Reset' (id='resetBtn') clears all customers, resets all statistics, and resets tellers to idle.
- Keyboard: press 'Space' to add a customer (same as button). Press 'P' to pause/resume the entire simulation clock. Press '1','2','3' to toggle individual tellers open/closed (closed teller turns gray 0x666666 and won't accept customers).

## HUD / Statistics Panel
- A semi-transparent dark panel (id='statsPanel') in the top-right corner showing:
  - Total Arrived (id='statArrived')
  - Total Served (id='statServed')
  - Queue Length (id='statQueueLen')
  - Avg Wait Time in seconds (id='statAvgWait')
  - Avg Service Time (id='statAvgService')
  - Utilization per teller as percentage (id='statUtil1', 'statUtil2', 'statUtil3')
  - Simulation Time (id='statSimTime')

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with the following fields updated every frame:
  - simulationRunning: boolean (true if not paused)
  - autoArrival: boolean (true if Poisson arrivals active)
  - arrivalRate: number (current lambda)
  - totalArrived: number
  - totalServed: number
  - queueLength: number (customers waiting in queue, not being served)
  - customersInScene: number (total customer meshes currently in scene)
  - avgWaitTime: number (seconds, 0 if none served yet)
  - avgServiceTime: number (seconds, 0 if none served yet)
  - tellerStates: array of 3 objects each with { open: boolean, busy: boolean, servingCustomerId: number|null, utilization: number }
  - activeParticles: number (current live particle count)
  - simulationTime: number (elapsed sim seconds)
  - lastEvent: string ('arrival'|'service_start'|'service_end'|'reset'|'none')
  - totalWaitTimeSum: number (sum of all wait times for averaging)
  - totalServiceTimeSum: number (sum of all service times for averaging)

Ensure the simulation uses requestAnimationFrame with delta time. All stats must update in real-time. The scene should be visually clear and the queue behavior must be correct FIFO ordering.
physics_constraints: Customers must follow FIFO queue discipline. Service times must be positive and drawn from exponential-like distribution (3-8s range). Arrival rate lambda controls Poisson process. Server utilization = busy_time / total_time per teller, bounded [0,1]. Conservation: totalArrived >= totalServed + queueLength + number_currently_being_served. Average wait time and service time must be non-negative and NaN-free. Particles must have finite lifetimes and be cleaned up.
